free_tier.stated: 'Upload your personal files to a secure cloud storage system ... You get 1 TB of space'.
free_tier.notes: The 1 TB claim is on the landing page and on its premium subdomain, which serve the same text.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated on the pages read

retention.stated: not stated on the pages read; the only related statement is that 'a premium user can restrict' access to their own files

egress.terms: Free download volume is not published by the vendor. A third-party leecher publishes a cap of 650 MB/day for the host, which is the only byte figure found.

interface_detail: Web upload and file manager on a subdomain (premium.isra.cloud). No API was found; the vendor publishes no endpoint.
tooling: Browser only as read. Both Leechall and PrimeLeech carry an isra.cloud generator, so a leecher is the only scripted pull found.
chaining: 1 TB of free storage is the headline, but a 650 MB/day pull makes it an archive that takes two years to drain. The paid tier is sold only through resellers, so the vendor's own checkout is not the cheapest route.

limits.value: 1 TB of storage on the free account
650 MB per day of download (third-party figure from leechall.com)
the vendor's terms say the daily rate 'can be changed in any case if decided by our Administration'

limits_note: The 1 TB is storage, not transfer. A free account can hold 1 TB and move 650 MB a day, so the ratio between the two is what makes the offer unusable as a transfer path.
binding_note: 650 MB/day is about 19.5 GB a month, which fails 1 TiB by a factor of 52. The storage figure never binds because the transfer figure is met first, every month.

identity_cost.detail: Free signup on the site. Premium is sold as a voucher code redeemed in My Account, bought from resellers including 24instant ('Official Reseller'), safedeal.cc and apseller - three different prices for the same 30 days.

reliability_note: The terms state the per-day allowance can be changed at the administration's discretion, and that a premium user's files may not be downloadable by another account even with premium.
confidence_note: The 1 TB free storage is the vendor's own sentence. The daily transfer cap is a third-party statement and the premium price is reseller-only, so the record's weakest load-bearing field is reported. A free account and a measured 24-hour pull would settle both.

evidence.proved: 'You get 1 TB of space' and the cross-platform sharing claim
third-party daily cap for the host: 'isra.cloud 0 B / 650 MB /d'
reseller prices labelled 'Official Reseller': 'Isra Cloud 30 Days Premium 20,00 €', 'Isra Cloud 90 Days Premium 52,00 €'
the daily allowance 'can be changed in any case if decided by our Administration' and the premium-file access restriction

price_per_tb_month: EUR 20 per 30 days (reseller); free tier is storage-heavy and transfer-poor
notes: The vendor has no pricing page: isra.cloud/premium and premium.isra.cloud both 404 or serve the landing text. Resellers disagree by 2x on the same 30 days (€20 at 24instant, €40 at safedeal), which is the strongest evidence that the vendor sells wholesale codes and does not publish a price.
